lines.text: Checkpoint one. Let's see how much of Phase 1 you remember.
lines.say: Checkpoint one. Let's see how much of Phase one you remember.

lines.text: Welcome to your first checkpoint: eight quick questions on lessons T01 to T04.
lines.say: Welcome to your first checkpoint: eight quick questions on lessons T one to T four.

lines.text: Read each question, pick an answer, and pause the video whenever you need more time.
lines.say: Read each question, pick an answer, and pause the video whenever you need more time.

lines.text: It's not graded. Missing one just shows you what to revisit.
lines.say: It's not graded. Missing one just shows you what to revisit.

lines.text: Question one, from T01. What is a cryptocurrency? Choose A, B, C or D.
lines.say: Question one, from T one. What is a cryptocurrency? Choose A, B, C or D.

lines.text: It's A. Crypto is a digital asset recorded on a shared public ledger: the blockchain.
lines.say: It's A. Crypto is a digital asset recorded on a shared public ledger: the blockchain.

lines.text: B is tempting, but your phone holds keys, not coins. The coins are entries on the ledger.
lines.say: B is tempting, but your phone holds keys, not coins. The coins are entries on the ledger.

lines.text: Question two, from T01. You hold 0.005 BTC, and one BTC costs 60,000 USDT. What is it worth?
lines.say: Question two, from T one. You hold zero point zero zero five B-T-C, and one B-T-C costs sixty thousand U-S-D-T. What is it worth?

lines.text: It's B, 300 USDT. Value is amount times price: 0.005 times 60,000.
lines.say: It's B, three hundred U-S-D-T. Value is amount times price: zero point zero zero five times sixty thousand.

lines.text: C is a decimal slip. 3,000 USDT is what 0.05 BTC would be worth, ten times more.
lines.say: C is a decimal slip. Three thousand U-S-D-T is what zero point zero five B-T-C would be worth, ten times more.

lines.text: Question three, from T02. Suddenly far more people want to buy than to sell. What tends to happen?
lines.say: Question three, from T two. Suddenly far more people want to buy than to sell. What tends to happen?

lines.text: A. Buyers compete for the few sellers and offer more, so the price tends to rise.
lines.say: A. Buyers compete for the few sellers and offer more, so the price tends to rise.

lines.text: But B is wrong: nothing is guaranteed. News or thin trading can turn the price quickly.
lines.say: But B is wrong: nothing is guaranteed. News or thin trading can turn the price quickly.

lines.text: Question four, from T02. What does high volatility mean?
lines.say: Question four, from T two. What does high volatility mean?

lines.text: It's B. Volatility is how far and how fast the price swings, up and down.
lines.say: It's B. Volatility is how far and how fast the price swings, up and down.

lines.text: A is a trap. A volatile price can fall just as sharply as it rises.
lines.say: A is a trap. A volatile price can fall just as sharply as it rises.

lines.text: Question five, from T03. In the pair BTC/USDT, which one is the base asset?
lines.say: Question five, from T three. In the pair B-T-C U-S-D-T, which one is the base asset?

lines.text: A, BTC. The base is the asset being priced: one BTC costs this many USDT.
lines.say: A, B-T-C. The base is the asset being priced: one B-T-C costs this many U-S-D-T.

lines.text: USDT is the quote, the unit of the price. It aims to track the dollar, with no guarantee.
lines.say: U-S-D-T is the quote, the unit of the price. It aims to track the dollar, with no guarantee.

lines.text: Question six, from T03. You buy 0.001 BTC when the price is 65,000 USDT. How many USDT is that?
lines.say: Question six, from T three. You buy zero point zero zero one B-T-C when the price is sixty-five thousand U-S-D-T. How many U-S-D-T is that?

lines.text: B, 65 USDT. Quantity times price: 0.001 times 65,000. That's the notional value.
lines.say: B, sixty-five U-S-D-T. Quantity times price: zero point zero zero one times sixty-five thousand. That's the notional value.

lines.text: D is the price of one whole BTC. You're buying one thousandth of a BTC.
lines.say: D is the price of one whole B-T-C. You're buying one thousandth of a B-T-C.

lines.text: Question seven, from T04. The best bid is 59,990 and the best ask is 60,010 USDT. The spread?
lines.say: Question seven, from T four. The best bid is fifty-nine thousand nine hundred ninety and the best ask is sixty thousand ten U-S-D-T. The spread?

lines.text: B, 20 USDT. The spread is the best ask minus the best bid: 60,010 minus 59,990.
lines.say: B, twenty U-S-D-T. The spread is the best ask minus the best bid: sixty thousand ten minus fifty-nine thousand nine hundred ninety.

lines.text: C is the bid itself: the highest price a buyer is offering right now. Not the gap.
lines.say: C is the bid itself: the highest price a buyer is offering right now. Not the gap.

lines.text: Question eight, from T04. A message asks for your OTP, the one-time code. What do you do?
lines.say: Question eight, from T four. A message asks for your O-T-P, the one-time code. What do you do?

lines.text: C. Never share it. Open the exchange app yourself, or use its official support page.
lines.say: C. Never share it. Open the exchange app yourself, or use its official support page.

lines.text: A is exactly what scammers want. Rushing you is a trick, and an OTP opens your account.
lines.say: A is exactly what scammers want. Rushing you is a trick, and an O-T-P opens your account.

lines.text: Before Phase 2, four safety points that matter most.
lines.say: Before Phase two, four safety points that matter most.

lines.text: An exchange is not a bank. Your balance there has no bank-style guarantee.
lines.say: An exchange is not a bank. Your balance there has no bank-style guarantee.

lines.text: Never share your password, OTP or API secret keys. Not even with someone claiming to be support.
lines.say: Never share your password, O-T-P or A-P-I secret keys. Not even with someone claiming to be support.

lines.text: USDT aims to track one US dollar, but that peg is not guaranteed.
lines.say: U-S-D-T aims to track one US dollar, but that peg is not guaranteed.

lines.text: And prices can swing fast. You can always choose to wait, and make no trade.
lines.say: And prices can swing fast. You can always choose to wait, and make no trade.

lines.text: Here's where each question came from.
lines.say: Here's where each question came from.

lines.text: Questions one and two: T01. Three and four: T02.
lines.say: Questions one and two: T one. Three and four: T two.

lines.text: Five and six: T03. Seven and eight: T04.
lines.say: Five and six: T three. Seven and eight: T four.

lines.say: Missed one? Rewatch that lesson before Phase two. There's no penalty, and you can retry anytime.
